from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title_text = "The Big Idea: From Smoothies to Ingredients"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Think of a complex signal like a mixed fruit smoothie.",
            "The Fourier Transform is the prism that finds the fruits.",
            "It breaks down complex waves into simple, pure notes.",
            "We move from the time domain to the frequency domain.",
            "This reveals the hidden ingredients inside any signal."
        ]
        
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors based on animation description
        COLOR_WAVE = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_SMOOTHIE = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_PRISM = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_R = "#FF0000"
        COLOR_G = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_B = "#0000FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a complex, white #FFFFFF wave.
        complex_wave = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * PI * x) + 0.3 * np.sin(5 * PI * x) + 0.2 * np.cos(10 * PI * x),
            x_range=[-1.0, 1.0],
            color=COLOR_WAVE
        )
        self.place_in_area(complex_wave, "B2", "D3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_WAVE),
            Create(complex_wave),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Transform wave into a light blue #ADD8E6 smoothie icon.
        smoothie_cup = Polygon([-0.4, -0.6, 0], [0.4, -0.6, 0], [0.5, 0.6, 0], [-0.5, 0.6, 0], 
                              color=COLOR_SMOOTHIE, fill_opacity=0.8)
        smoothie_top = Arc(radius=0.5, start_angle=0, angle=PI, 
                           color=COLOR_SMOOTHIE, fill_opacity=1).move_to([0, 0.6, 0])
        straw = Line([0.1, 0.6, 0], [0.3, 1.1, 0], color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        smoothie = VGroup(smoothie_cup, smoothie_top, straw)
        self.place_in_area(smoothie, "B2", "D3", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_SMOOTHIE),
            ReplacementTransform(complex_wave, smoothie),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display a yellow #FFFF00 triangle labeled "Mathematical Prism".
        prism = Triangle(color=COLOR_PRISM, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(prism, "C4", "D4", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        prism_label = Text("Mathematical Prism", font_size=18, color=COLOR_PRISM)
        # Position label exactly one grid unit below the prism area to ensure association
        self.place_at_grid(prism_label, "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_PRISM),
            FadeIn(prism),
            Write(prism_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Move smoothie through the prism.
        prism_center = (self.grid["C4"] + self.grid["D4"]) / 2
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_SMOOTHIE),
            smoothie.animate.move_to(prism_center).scale(0.5).set_opacity(0.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Show three colored waves: red #FF0000, green #00FF00, blue #0000FF.
        wave_r = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * x), x_range=[-0.8, 0.8], color=COLOR_R)
        wave_g = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.3 * np.sin(5 * PI * x), x_range=[-0.8, 0.8], color=COLOR_G)
        wave_b = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.2 * np.sin(10 * PI * x), x_range=[-0.8, 0.8], color=COLOR_B)
        
        waves = VGroup(wave_r, wave_g, wave_b).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        # Position on the right side of the grid
        self.place_in_area(waves, "B5", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_G),
            FadeOut(smoothie),
            FadeOut(prism),
            FadeOut(prism_label),
            Create(waves),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title = "Prerequisite: The Harmony of Sine Waves"
        lines = [
            "Every complex periodic shape is built from simple sine waves.",
            "By adding waves of different frequencies, new shapes emerge.",
            "These building blocks combine to create the harmony we see."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        RED_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        BLUE_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        WHITE_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # Time tracker for synchronized oscillations
        time_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        self.add(time_tracker)
        time_tracker.add_updater(lambda m, dt: m.increment_value(dt))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Description: Show three dots (red, green, blue) oscillating.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        dot_red = Dot(color=RED_COLOR)
        dot_green = Dot(color=GREEN_COLOR)
        dot_blue = Dot(color=BLUE_COLOR)
        
        # Position dots in Column 2 (Rows B, C, D)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_red, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_green, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(dot_blue, "D2")
        
        # Capture baseline positions for updaters
        pos_red = dot_red.get_center().copy()
        pos_green = dot_green.get_center().copy()
        pos_blue = dot_blue.get_center().copy()
        
        # Add updaters for oscillation (vertical)
        dot_red.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(pos_red + UP * 0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * 0.5 * time_tracker.get_value())))
        dot_green.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(pos_green + UP * 0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * 1.0 * time_tracker.get_value())))
        dot_blue.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(pos_blue + UP * 0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * 1.5 * time_tracker.get_value())))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_red), FadeIn(dot_green), FadeIn(dot_blue))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Description: Overlay the three corresponding sine waves.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create VMobjects for waves
        wave_red = VMobject(color=RED_COLOR)
        wave_green = VMobject(color=GREEN_COLOR)
        wave_blue = VMobject(color=BLUE_COLOR)
        
        # Place waves in areas (Rows B, C, D; Columns 2 to 6)
        self.place_in_area(wave_red, "B2", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(wave_green, "C2", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(wave_blue, "D2", "D6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Baseline centers for the updater logic
        c_red = wave_red.get_center().copy()
        c_green = wave_green.get_center().copy()
        c_blue = wave_blue.get_center().copy()
        
        # Function to generate points for a moving sine wave centered at 'center'
        def get_wave_points(center, freq, amp, t, width=4.0):
            res = 60
            x_vals = np.linspace(-width/2, width/2, res)
            return [center + np.array([x, amp * np.sin(2 * PI * freq * (t - x)), 0]) for x in x_vals]

        # Add updaters to VMobjects to avoid creating new objects each frame
        wave_red.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(c_red, 0.5, 0.4, time_tracker.get_value())))
        wave_green.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(c_green, 1.0, 0.4, time_tracker.get_value())))
        wave_blue.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(get_wave_points(c_blue, 1.5, 0.4, time_tracker.get_value())))
        
        self.play(Create(wave_red), Create(wave_green), Create(wave_blue))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Description: Sum the waves into one jagged white path.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create a VMobject for the combined wave
        sum_wave = VMobject(color=WHITE_COLOR, stroke_width=4)
        # Place in a larger area (Rows E and F, Columns 2 to 6)
        self.place_in_area(sum_wave, "F2", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        c_sum = sum_wave.get_center().copy()
        
        # Function to generate points for the summation of the three sine waves
        def get_sum_points(center, t, width=4.0):
            res = 100
            x_vals = np.linspace(-width/2, width/2, res)
            points = []
            for x in x_vals:
                y = (0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * 0.5 * (t - x)) + 
                     0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * 1.0 * (t - x)) + 
                     0.4 * np.sin(2 * PI * 1.5 * (t - x)))
                points.append(center + np.array([x, y, 0]))
            return points
            
        sum_wave.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_points_as_corners(get_sum_points(c_sum, time_tracker.get_value())))
        
        # Label centered above the sum wave
        sum_label = Text("Summed Result", font_size=24, color=WHITE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(sum_label, "E2", "E6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(sum_wave), Write(sum_label))
        self.wait(4)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Imagine wrapping our signal around a central circular origin.",
            "We spin the signal at different test frequencies.",
            "If frequencies don't match, the shape stays centered.",
            "When they match, the center of mass shifts dramatically.",
            "This shift flags a hidden frequency in our signal."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Winding Machine: Visualizing the Math", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define colors from storyboard
        signal_color = "#FFFFFF"
        circle_color = "#808080"
        vector_color = "#00FFFF"
        com_color = "#FF00FF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Imagine wrapping our signal around a central circular origin.
        # Display a white #FFFFFF signal wave.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(signal_color)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1.2, 1.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=1.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False, "stroke_width": 2, "color": GRAY}
        )
        
        f_signal = 2.0  # 2Hz signal
        signal_graph = axes.plot(lambda t: np.cos(2 * np.pi * f_signal * t), color=signal_color)
        signal_label = Text("f(t)", color=signal_color, font_size=24)
        
        signal_group = VGroup(axes, signal_graph)
        # Use place_in_area to center the signal in the top-right quadrant
        self.place_in_area(signal_group, "B2", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        # Use next_to for logical visual association (L003)
        signal_label.next_to(signal_group, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(signal_graph), Write(signal_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We spin the signal at different test frequencies.
        # Draw a gray #808080 circle below the wave.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(circle_color)
        
        # Center of the winding visualization in the bottom-right
        winding_origin = self.grid["E4"]
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=circle_color, stroke_width=2).move_to(winding_origin)
        
        self.play(Create(circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # If frequencies don't match, the shape stays centered.
        # Wrap the signal around the circle in white #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(signal_color)
        
        f_test = ValueTracker(0.5) # Start with a mismatching frequency
        
        # Helper to generate the wrapped signal curve
        # z(t) = (f(t) + offset) * e^(-i * 2pi * f_test * t)
        def get_wrapped_signal_path(f):
            return ParametricFunction(
                lambda t: winding_origin + np.array([
                    (np.cos(2 * np.pi * f_signal * t) + 1.5) * np.cos(-2 * np.pi * f * t) * 0.4,
                    (np.cos(2 * np.pi * f_signal * t) + 1.5) * np.sin(-2 * np.pi * f * t) * 0.4,
                    0
                ]),
                t_range=[0, 4, 0.05],
                color=signal_color
            )
            
        wrapped_signal = always_redraw(lambda: get_wrapped_signal_path(f_test.get_value()))
        
        self.play(Create(wrapped_signal))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # When they match, the center of mass shifts dramatically.
        # Add a cyan #00FFFF vector rotating at a variable frequency.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(vector_color)
        
        t_curr = ValueTracker(0)
        # Vector pointing to the current point on the winding curve
        vector = always_redraw(lambda: Arrow(
            start=winding_origin,
            end=winding_origin + np.array([
                (np.cos(2 * np.pi * f_signal * t_curr.get_value()) + 1.5) * np.cos(-2 * np.pi * f_test.get_value() * t_curr.get_value()) * 0.4,
                (np.cos(2 * np.pi * f_signal * t_curr.get_value()) + 1.5) * np.sin(-2 * np.pi * f_test.get_value() * t_curr.get_value()) * 0.4,
                0
            ]),
            buff=0,
            color=vector_color,
            stroke_width=4
        ))
        
        self.add(vector)
        # Animate the vector spinning
        self.play(t_curr.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        # Sweep the test frequency to match the signal frequency (resonance)
        self.play(f_test.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This shift flags a hidden frequency in our signal.
        # Show a magenta #FF00FF dot at the shape's center of mass.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(com_color)
        
        # Function to calculate center of mass position based on frequency
        def get_com_pos(f):
            ts = np.linspace(0, 4, 200)
            xs = (np.cos(2 * np.pi * f_signal * ts) + 1.5) * np.cos(-2 * np.pi * f * ts) * 0.4
            ys = (np.cos(2 * np.pi * f_signal * ts) + 1.5) * np.sin(-2 * np.pi * f * ts) * 0.4
            return winding_origin + np.array([np.mean(xs), np.mean(ys), 0])

        com_dot = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(get_com_pos(f_test.get_value()), color=com_color, radius=0.1))
        com_label = Text("Center of Mass", font_size=16, color=com_color)
        # Keep label attached to dot using updater (L011/L014 safe as it's property modification)
        com_label.add_updater(lambda m: m.next_to(com_dot, RIGHT, buff=0.1))

        self.play(FadeIn(com_dot), Write(com_label))
        
        # Demonstrate the shift again by changing frequency away and back
        self.play(f_test.animate.set_value(0.5), run_time=2)
        self.play(f_test.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=2)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Title and lecture lines
        title_str = "The Frequency Spectrum: The Recipe Card"
        lines = [
            "We plot these shifts to create a frequency spectrum.",
            "The horizontal axis represents the test frequencies used.",
            "Vertical bars show the strength of each frequency component.",
            "This spectrum is the recipe card for our signal.",
            "It stays steady even when the signal looks chaotic."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)
        
        # Colors
        RED_COLOR = "#FF0000"
        GREEN_COLOR = "#00FF00"
        BLUE_COLOR = "#0000FF"
        GLOW_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: "We plot these shifts to create a frequency spectrum."
        # Animation: Draw a white #FFFFFF horizontal frequency axis.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Frequency axis (Horizontal)
        # Using Col 3 to 6 to stay away from Column 1/2 for labels.
        freq_axis = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["E3"], 
            end=self.grid["E6"] + RIGHT*0.2, 
            color=WHITE, 
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        # Strength axis (Vertical)
        amp_axis = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["E3"], 
            end=self.grid["B3"] + UP*0.2, 
            color=WHITE, 
            buff=0,
            stroke_width=4
        )
        
        self.play(Create(freq_axis), Create(amp_axis), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: "The horizontal axis represents the test frequencies used."
        # Animation: Create a tall red #FF0000 spike at a low frequency.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED_COLOR)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define lecture lines for Section 6
        lecture_lines = [
            "Time and frequency domains show the same information differently.",
            "The Fourier Transform is the bridge between these views.",
            "It reveals the simple structure within our complex world."
        ]
        
        # Initialize layout
        self.setup_layout("Summary: One World, Two Views", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visual styling
        TIME_COLOR = BLUE_C
        FREQ_COLOR = ORANGE
        BRIDGE_COLOR = "#FFD700"  # Gold as requested

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # L1: Time and frequency domains show the same information differently.
        # Step: Show "Time" (left) and "Frequency" (right) labels.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        time_label = Text("Time Domain", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        freq_label = Text("Frequency Domain", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        
        # Position labels at B2 and B5 (distance 1 unit from visual content below)
        self.place_at_grid(time_label, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(freq_label, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            Write(time_label),
            Write(freq_label),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # L2: The Fourier Transform is the bridge between these views.
        # Step: Display a beating heart wave and a single spike.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Create Heart Wave (Time Domain)
        ecg_pts = [
            [-0.5, 0, 0], [-0.3, 0, 0], [-0.25, 0.1, 0], [-0.2, 0, 0],
            [-0.15, -0.1, 0], [-0.1, 0.6, 0], [-0.05, -0.2, 0], [0, 0, 0],
            [0.1, 0.2, 0], [0.2, 0, 0], [0.5, 0, 0]
        ]
        heart_wave = VMobject(color=TIME_COLOR)
        heart_wave.set_points_as_corners([np.array(p) for p in ecg_pts])
        
        # Create Single Spike (Frequency Domain)
        spike_pts = [
            [-0.5, 0, 0], [-0.05, 0, 0], [0, 0.8, 0], [0.05, 0, 0], [0.5, 0, 0]
        ]
        spike = VMobject(color=FREQ_COLOR)
        spike.set_points_as_corners([np.array(p) for p in spike_pts])
        
        # Position graphs in Row C (1 grid unit below Row B labels)
        self.place_at_grid(heart_wave, 'C2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(spike, 'C5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            Create(heart_wave),
            Create(spike),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # L3: It reveals the simple structure within our complex world.
        # Step: Draw a gold #FFD700 bridge arrow between the views.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BRIDGE_COLOR)
        
        # Bridge Arrow connecting the two domains
        bridge_arrow = DoubleArrow(
            start=self.grid['C3'],
            end=self.grid['C4'],
            color=BRIDGE_COLOR,
            stroke_width=4,
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        # Bridge Label
        ft_text = Text("Fourier Transform", font_size=18, color=BRIDGE_COLOR)
        self.place_in_area(ft_text, 'B3', 'B4', scale_factor=0.8) # Above the arrow, centered between B3 and B4
        
        self.play(
            GrowFromCenter(bridge_arrow),
            FadeIn(ft_text),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Unveiling the Fourier Transform: The Mathematical Prism

sections.title: The Big Idea: From Smoothies to Ingredients
sections.content: Introduce the concept of decomposition. Just as a smoothie can be broken down into its original fruits, complex signals can be broken down into simple waves. This section establishes the 'Why'—moving from the Time Domain (how things change over time) to the Frequency Domain (the underlying ingredients).
sections.example: Imagine a 'Music-Bot' character listening to a messy sound wave. The bot uses a 'Mathematical Prism' to see that the mess is actually just three pure notes played at once: C, E, and G.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Harmony of Sine Waves
sections.content: Explain the concept of superposition. Any complex periodic shape can be built by adding up simple sine and cosine waves of different frequencies and amplitudes. This provides the 'Building Blocks' needed to understand the transform.
sections.example: Visualizing three 'Oscillating Snakes' of different speeds. When they crawl on top of each other, their combined path creates a jagged, complex mountain range shape.

sections.title: The Winding Machine: Visualizing the Math
sections.content: Introduce the intuition behind the Fourier Transform formula. Instead of just showing the integral, visualize 'wrapping' the signal around a circle. If the wrapping frequency matches a hidden frequency in the signal, the 'Center of Mass' of the shape shifts away from the origin.
sections.example: A 'Mechanical Winder' device. As it spins a signal at 440Hz (an 'A' note), a weight on the wheel suddenly swings wildly to one side, signaling that the 'ingredient' has been found.

sections.title: The Frequency Spectrum: The Recipe Card
sections.content: Translate the 'Center of Mass' findings into a graph. The horizontal axis represents Frequency, and the vertical axis represents Amplitude (Strength). This is the 'Frequency Domain'—a static 'recipe' for the dynamic signal.
sections.example: A 'Digital Equalizer' on a stereo. While the music waves (Time Domain) dance frantically, the bars (Frequency Domain) stay relatively steady, showing which frequencies are dominating the mix.

sections.title: Real-World Magic: Applications
sections.content: Showcase how this math is used in modern technology. Focus on data compression and noise filtering. Explain that by 'deleting' high-frequency noise or unimportant details in the frequency domain, we can clean signals and shrink files.
sections.example: A 'Noise-Cancelling Robot' in a noisy factory. The robot 'transforms' the noise, identifies the constant hum frequency, and mathematically deletes it so it can hear a human's voice clearly.

sections.title: Summary: One World, Two Views
sections.content: Consolidate the lesson. Reiterate that the Time Domain and Frequency Domain are just two ways of looking at the same information. The Fourier Transform is the bridge between them.
sections.example: A split-screen view: on the left, a heart monitor's rhythmic 'beep' (Time); on the right, a single sharp peak at 1.2Hz (Frequency). Both represent the same beating heart.
